notes: Published L., D., VI, Bl. 3, no. 9; photo Berlin Academy 719. All 13 type lines (stone lines 1-16) are on p. 39; Griffith's commentary follows on pp. 39-40. He renders the opening 'The mother of Malêqêrebar the king, Lakhizamani' (tdḫe = mother's parentage word), takes the text for a letter from the queen-mother or a description of a mission from Meroë whose lines 'contain many numerals', and translates ll. 5-6 'Isis in Philae, one khe, Isis in Tebawe (Abaton), one khe', l. 7 'Isis and Horus(?)', l. 10 '(Figures of) Osiris in Philae', l. 11 'Osiris in Tebawe', ll. 12-13 'Isis in Philae', 'Isis in Tebawe', l. 15 'The khabkhen of the king, Mashtaraq'; the last word yetebḫe matches the hieroglyphic word that ends gods' legends ('give'?). He equates yni (l. 12) with the two-stroke yini of l. 11. Numerals: single and double strokes are {1} and {2}; the hook sign and the group of < with two slanted strokes are written {⌐} and {<}{⫽} (value not given; dropped from text_corpus). Words cut by a type-line break are joined (lẖidmni, pilqeteli, tebaweteli). Spaces as printed (gaps measured): tebwe(14)teli and tebwetel are single words in the type. Griffith's '?' stands over the t before šdrte (l. 8) and over the š of ašy (l. 14). My doubts: the first a of akeñ (a cramped a-sign, a stroke over the 2) and the two-stroke y of yini.
